topics.title: Right to Information (RTI)
topics.description: The Right to Information Act, 2005 allows Indian citizens to request information from public authorities. Any citizen can file an RTI application to get information about government activities, decisions, and policies.
examples: You can file an RTI to know why your application was rejected or to get details of government contracts.

topics.title: Consumer Rights
topics.description: Consumer protection laws in India protect consumers from unfair trade practices, defective products, and deficient services. Consumers have the right to seek redressal for grievances.
examples: If you buy a defective product, you can file a complaint with the consumer forum within 2 years of purchase.

topics.title: Property Rights
topics.description: Property rights in India are governed by various laws including the Transfer of Property Act, 1882. Property can be acquired through purchase, inheritance, or gift.
examples: Property transactions must be registered with the sub-registrar's office to be legally valid.

topics.title: Employment Rights
topics.description: Indian labor laws protect employees' rights including minimum wages, working hours, leave entitlements, and protection against unfair dismissal.
examples: Employees are entitled to paid leave, overtime compensation, and cannot be terminated without proper notice.

topics.title: Domestic Violence
topics.description: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 protects women from physical, emotional, sexual, and economic abuse within the household.
relevant_laws: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
examples: A woman can file a complaint with the protection officer or directly approach the magistrate for relief.
